clue.text: Conservative - first member to join afresh in game - was most often 12 9

definitions.note: a verb phrase describing the person; the answer is the person who did it

indicators.note: doing something afresh means making it anew, so the letters are put together in a new order
the built-up letters are placed inside the following game word

blocks.note: a stick-and-ball game, which opens around the other letters
A as in A1, first class
the four letters of join rearranged

explanation.surface: A Tory politician, newly signed up to a sport, turns out to be its most frequent winner.
explanation.walkthrough: A for first comes from A1, first class. The definition leans on 12 9, FIRST PAST THE POST: the title goes to the rider with most wins in a season.
explanation.definitionFit: In British horse racing the title goes to the rider who records the most winners over a season, i.e. most often finished first.

clue.text: Tom and Jerry's performance passed by anti-suffragettes

blocks.note: first meaning: the routine of a cartoon cat chasing a mouse
second meaning: the 1913 law nicknamed for how it released and re-arrested hunger-striking suffragettes

explanation.surface: A cartoon double act set beside a piece of parliamentary history.
explanation.walkthrough: The Prisoners (Temporary Discharge for Ill-Health) Act of 1913 let the government free starving suffragettes and re-imprison them once recovered, a game of cat and mouse.
explanation.definitionFit: The cartoon pair stage an endless chase routine, and the nickname of the 1913 statute described exactly that kind of pursuit.

clue.text: Fury in Bremerhaven, Germany

indicators.note: says the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

blocks.note: letters running across the end of the port name and the start of the country

explanation.surface: A sudden rage breaks out in a north German port.
explanation.definitionFit: The Furies of Greek myth were spirits of vengeance, so a Fury is a punishing pursuer of wrongdoers.

clue.text: Word of a sort the church has to utter

blocks.note: a kind of word, a part of speech

explanation.surface: A church insists on a particular form of words being spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to speak or articulate words aloud, or to declare formally.

clue.text: Excluded by Oxford to conform?

blocks.note: to conform is to fit in

explanation.surface: Someone shut out by the university for refusing to toe the line.
explanation.definitionFit: Being left out of things or not included is an informal sense of the phrase, as in feeling sidelined.

clue.text: Injection of Irish-American waders from Brazil

explanation.surface: Vaccinating Irish-American birdwatchers' quarry in South America.
explanation.definitionFit: Jabirus are large storks of Central and South America, long-legged birds that stalk through marshes.

clue.text: It isn't fair to give temperature in Celsius

definitions.note: a clause describing the answer, which is a noun for something or someone unfair

blocks.note: C is the symbol for Celsius

explanation.surface: A complaint that quoting temperatures in Celsius is unfair.
explanation.walkthrough: The temperature is read as being stated in C, so C comes first, then HEAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A swindle or a person who breaks the rules is unfair, dishonest dealing.

clue.text: Cry over what was staked by former partner

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: Weeping over a stake an ex-partner put down.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' can mean placed above, so the former partner comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: To call out suddenly in surprise or emotion is a verb sense of cry.

clue.text: King's head fits awkwardly with fireguard

definitions.note: possessive; the answer is a title belonging to the King

indicators.note: something put together awkwardly is jumbled, so these letters are disordered

blocks.note: the two words as written, to be shuffled
a fender is a low guard round a fireplace

explanation.surface: A monarch's head fits badly beside the fireplace guard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King's head' reads as one phrase but splits: King's is the definition and head joins fits as fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Fidei Defensor, Defender of the Faith, is a title borne by English monarchs since Henry VIII, so it is the King's.

clue.text: See 12
Ascribe unrest to Italian city

indicators.note: unrest is disturbance, so the word before it is stirred up

explanation.surface: Blaming civil disorder on a particular town in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Brescia is a city in Lombardy, northern Italy, at the foot of the Alps.

clue.text: Black note held by fiddler

indicators.note: something held is gripped inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: the emperor said to have fiddled while Rome burned

explanation.surface: A dark note played on a violinist's instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: Nero fiddling while Rome burned is the classic crossword fiddler.
explanation.definitionFit: Negro is the Spanish and Italian word for the colour black, and a dated term for a black person.

clue.text: "Winner takes all" - see complete article in "Bugle Call"

indicators.note: the middle words are placed inside the bugle call, splitting it in two

blocks.note: first half of the military bugle call sounded before Last Post
second half of the same call

explanation.surface: A cross-reference telling the reader to find the full story in a newspaper called Bugle Call.
explanation.walkthrough: First Post is the British military bugle call that precedes Last Post at the end of a soldier's day.
explanation.definitionFit: The electoral system gives each seat to whoever polls most votes, with nothing for runners-up, hence winner takes all.

clue.text: Lebanese Christians make horses go round on it

indicators.note: going round something means encircling it, so one piece wraps the other

explanation.surface: Horses being ridden round a carousel by worshippers in Lebanon.
explanation.definitionFit: The Maronite Church is an Eastern Catholic body centred in Lebanon, whose members form a large Christian community there.

clue.text: Pooh's work for the Guardian? The answer's in the soil

definitions.note: a phrase describing where the answer is found

blocks.note: Winnie-the-Pooh composes little songs he calls hums
the newspaper speaks of itself as we and us

explanation.surface: Wondering whether the bear's songs were written for this newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue appeared in The Guardian, which would call itself US.
explanation.definitionFit: Humus is the dark organic matter formed from decayed plants, a component found within earth.

clue.text: Head start for image enhancer or head sweeper?

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter only

blocks.note: the opening letter of this word

explanation.surface: Choosing between a photo-retouching tool and a broom for the head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head start' looks like an idiom for an advantage, but it means the first letter of Head.
explanation.definitionFit: A brush passed over the scalp to tidy it is playfully called something that sweeps the head.

clue.text: Too much to be paid to international body?

explanation.surface: Asking whether an excessive sum is owed to a global organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: Undue means excessive or unwarranted, beyond what is appropriate.

clue.text: Useless fellow gone off in a huff

indicators.note: food gone off has spoiled, so the word before it is in a spoiled order

blocks.note: a dud is a useless thing or person

explanation.surface: A worthless man storms off in a sulk.
explanation.definitionFit: Dudgeon is a feeling of offended resentment, as in the idiom 'in high dudgeon'.

clue.text: Girth of one embracing the United Reform Church

indicators.note: to embrace is to hug, holding something within one's arms

explanation.surface: The size of a single person wrapping their arms round a Nonconformist church.
explanation.definitionFit: A surcingle is a strap passed round a horse's body to secure a saddle or blanket, a kind of girth.

clue.text: Likedown Jerry, slippery customers climb over little Tom

definitions.note: adjective phrase; the clue as given has likely lost a '1' from 'Like 1 down Jerry'

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means going upwards, so the word is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: a kit or kitten is a young cat; a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: Eels slither up past a small cat in a cartoon chase.
explanation.walkthrough: Sleekit is Scots for sly or sleek, famous from Burns's 'wee, sleekit, cow'rin, tim'rous beastie', a mouse, like Jerry of the 1-down cartoon.
explanation.definitionFit: Burns describes his field mouse with this Scots adjective, so it suits Jerry, the cartoon mouse.

clue.text: Agent of typhus with fatal reproduction

indicators.note: its tail, production, means a fresh staging, so the letters are put on anew in another order

blocks.note: the first two letters, split off from the rest of the word

explanation.surface: A carrier of a deadly disease that breeds lethally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reproduction' looks like one word for breeding but splits into RE plus production, the shuffle signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The parasite living on rats transmits murine typhus to humans, so it carries the disease.

clue.text: Real time left to the public

blocks.note: gen is genuine information, the real thing
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Live footage passed on to the people.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's 'caviare to the general' in Hamlet uses the word to mean the common people.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, 'the general' is an old literary term for ordinary people, the populace as a whole.

clue.text: The last people to enter anything as quality assurance?

definitions.note: read as two descriptions: a natural quality and a kind of life assurance

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so the people word is placed within the next word

blocks.note: the end is the last part

explanation.surface: Asking whether the final inspectors are those who check quality.
explanation.walkthrough: OWT is Yorkshire and Lancashire dialect for anything. An endowment policy is British life assurance paying out a lump sum at a set date.
explanation.definitionFit: An endowment is a natural gift or talent, and an endowment policy is a form of life assurance.

clue.text: Get rid of the liquid sound of the bells

indicators.note: says the answer is what is heard, not what is written

blocks.note: bells ring, and the twisting verb is said the same way

explanation.surface: Draining away a fluid that sounds like church bells.
explanation.definitionFit: To twist wet cloth so as to squeeze the water out is to remove its moisture.

clue.text: Begin wild party

indicators.note: something wild is out of control, so the letters run riot

explanation.surface: An instruction to kick off a raucous celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: A binge is a spree of heavy drinking or eating, a wild celebration.

clue.text: Finch to mediate on what to write with

blocks.note: chew on is to ponder; the printed word is probably meant to be meditate

explanation.surface: A bird told to reflect on its writing materials.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mediate on' reads best as meditate on, which is to chew on or ponder.
explanation.definitionFit: The chewink is the eastern towhee, a North American bird of the bunting and sparrow family once grouped with finches.

clue.text: Gallery would shortly be having boards for ventilation

indicators.note: said shortly means abbreviated, with most of the word dropped

blocks.note: would shrinks to 'd, as in I'd

explanation.surface: An art gallery soon to have slatted panels fitted for air.
explanation.definitionFit: A louvred window or door has sloping slats that let air through while keeping out rain and light.

clue.text: Think differently about German composer's role reversal: 17, say?

indicators.note: thinking differently means rearranging, so the word before is reordered
about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go round the next piece
a reversal turns something back to front, so the word before is read backwards

blocks.note: taken as written before being turned round

explanation.surface: Rethinking a German composer's part, playing it the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 is SURCINGLE, which can be heard as 'Sir Single': an unmarried man who is a Sir.
explanation.definitionFit: A knight bachelor holds the plain rank of knighthood outside any order; a bachelor is single, and a knight is a Sir.
